title: A shrinking expression-lane point edit needs the destructive authority it actually exercises

needles:
a shorter list
                // retires every point it omits
a non-destructive writer is refused a lane edit that drops points
Splitting the command is half the job

a reducer that retires
an identity belongs to a `Remove`-declared command

installed_sdk.rationale: No installed header, entry point, or SDK type changes. SetMidiExpressionLanePoints keeps its declared Note/Modify authority and its payload shape; what changes is the authority required_authorities derives from that payload inside the session translation unit. Claiming an installed-SDK surface would advertise a type that did not move.

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: The CLI registers the editor profile, which holds every destructive intent, so no CLI verb's verdict changes. No verb is added, removed, or re-gated.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: pulp_timeline_command_apply defaults to the proposal profile and will now refuse a set_midi_expression_lane_points whose replacement omits a point, but the tool schema states only that the default is non-destructive; it does not say which payloads a given profile may carry, and there is no operation that reports in advance whether an edit retires an identity. A caller still discovers the verdict by submitting. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).

live_product_control.rationale: Product A live timeline authority is absent for the sequencer generally, so neither the tightened refusal nor the edits that remain admitted is reachable as a live control. Owner: NW-D, and only where that source is Pulp-owned.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: No agent-capability row states which payloads a proposal writer may carry, so an agent cannot ask whether a point edit it is about to author will be admitted before submitting it. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).
